senses.en: a very large round object in space that moves around a star such as the Sun
examples: Mars is the **planet** that people talk about most.
Eight **planets** travel around the Sun.
Could there be life on another **planet**?

planet.note: The names of planets are capitalised: *Mars*, *Venus*, *Jupiter*. We usually write **Earth** with a capital letter when we mean the planet, but *the earth* when we mean the ground or soil.

senses.en: the curved path that a planet, moon or spacecraft follows around a larger object in space
examples: The Moon takes about 27 days to complete one **orbit** of the Earth.
The satellite is now in **orbit** above us.
Each planet has its own **orbit** around the Sun.

senses.en: to travel in a curved path around a planet, star or moon
examples: The space station **orbits** the Earth sixteen times a day.
Two small moons **orbit** Mars.
The telescope has been **orbiting** our planet since 1990.

orbit.note: As a verb, **orbit** takes an object with no preposition: *orbit the Earth* (not ~~orbit around the Earth~~). As a noun, use **in orbit** or *an orbit around something*.

senses.en: the natural force that pulls objects towards each other, and pulls things on Earth down to the ground
examples: Things fall to the ground because of **gravity**.
The Moon has much weaker **gravity** than the Earth.
Astronauts float because there is almost no **gravity** in the space station.

forms.vi: thuộc về trọng lực, hấp dẫn
forms.ex: The **gravitational** pull of the Moon moves the sea.

gravity.note: **Gravity** is uncountable, so we never say ~~a gravity~~ or ~~gravities~~. Say *there is no gravity* or *the force of gravity*.

senses.en: the layer of gases that surrounds a planet
examples: The Earth's **atmosphere** protects us from the Sun.
The **atmosphere** on Mars is very thin.
The spacecraft burned as it entered the **atmosphere**.

senses.en: the feeling or mood that a place or situation gives you
senses.vi: bầu không khí, không khí (nơi chốn)
examples: The little café has a warm, friendly **atmosphere**.
There was an exciting **atmosphere** before the launch.
I love the **atmosphere** of the night market.

atmosphere.note: Stress the first syllable: **AT**-mos-phere. The adjective is *atmospheric*.

senses.en: a gas in the air that has no colour or smell and that people, animals and plants need to live
examples: Humans cannot live without **oxygen**.
Astronauts carry **oxygen** in their suits.
There is not enough **oxygen** on Mars for us to breathe.

oxygen.note: **Oxygen** is uncountable: say *some oxygen* or *a lot of oxygen*, never ~~an oxygen~~. Stress the first syllable: **OX**-y-gen.

senses.en: good enough for people or animals to live in
examples: Scientists are looking for a **habitable** planet.
After the storm, the old house was no longer **habitable**.
Only a small part of the desert is **habitable**.

forms.en: the natural place where a plant or animal lives
forms.ex: Pollution is destroying the **habitat** of these birds.

forms.en: to live in a particular place
forms.ex: No one knows whether any creature **inhabits** that planet.
Venus is far too hot and is completely **uninhabitable**.

habitable.note: Careful: **inhabitable** means the *same* as habitable, not the opposite. The opposite is **uninhabitable**.

senses.en: the outside or top layer of something
examples: The **surface** of the Moon is covered with dust and rocks.
Water covers most of the Earth's **surface**.
Please clean the **surface** of the table before you eat.

senses.en: to come up to the top of the water from below
examples: The whale **surfaced** a few metres from our boat.
He swam down and then **surfaced** near the rocks.
The submarine **surfaces** once a day.

senses.en: a tube-shaped instrument that makes faraway things, especially stars and planets, look bigger and nearer
examples: We looked at Saturn through a **telescope**.
The school has a small **telescope** on the roof.
A powerful space **telescope** took these pictures.

telescope.note: Built from *tele-* (far) + *-scope* (an instrument for looking), like **television** and **telephone**.

senses.en: a person who is trained to travel and work in a spacecraft
senses.vi: phi hành gia, nhà du hành vũ trụ
examples: The **astronauts** spent six months on the space station.
She wants to become an **astronaut** one day.
An **astronaut** must wear a special suit outside the spacecraft.

astronaut.note: Russian space travellers are often called **cosmonauts**, and Chinese ones **taikonauts**, but *astronaut* is the general word in English.

senses.en: a vehicle that travels in space, with or without people inside
examples: The **spacecraft** landed safely in the sea.
Two **spacecraft** are now travelling towards Jupiter.
Engineers are testing a new **spacecraft** this year.

spacecraft.note: **Spacecraft** has the same form in the plural: *one spacecraft, two spacecraft* (never ~~spacecrafts~~). *Spaceship* is a more informal word and its plural is *spaceships*.

senses.en: connected with life or things from outside the planet Earth
senses.vi: ngoài Trái Đất, ngoài hành tinh
examples: Scientists are still searching for **extraterrestrial** life.
There is no clear proof of **extraterrestrial** visitors.
The film is about an **extraterrestrial** creature.

senses.en: a living being that comes from a planet other than Earth
examples: In the story, a friendly **extraterrestrial** lands in a garden.
Do you believe **extraterrestrials** really exist?

forms.en: short form of extraterrestrial, often used in films and newspapers
forms.vi: sinh vật ngoài hành tinh (viết tắt)
forms.ex: The famous film **ET** is about a lost alien.

forms.en: connected with the Earth or with land
forms.vi: thuộc về Trái Đất, trên cạn
forms.ex: Turtles lay their eggs in **terrestrial** nests on the beach.

extraterrestrial.note: A useful word-building word: *extra-* means **outside** and *terrestrial* means **of the Earth**, so extraterrestrial = *from outside the Earth*. Compare *extraordinary* = outside the ordinary.

senses.en: a living being that comes from another planet
senses.vi: người ngoài hành tinh, sinh vật ngoài hành tinh
examples: The boy dreamed that **aliens** landed in his school yard.
Nobody has ever met an **alien**.
In the film, the **alien** speaks perfect English.

senses.en: strange and completely unfamiliar to you
examples: At first, life in the big city felt **alien** to her.
The customs of the village were **alien** to the visitors.

alien.note: As a noun, **alien** usually means a being from space in everyday English and in films. As an adjective it more often means *unfamiliar or strange*, and it is followed by **to**: *the idea was alien to me*.

senses.en: any living thing that can move, such as an animal or an imaginary being
examples: Strange **creatures** live at the bottom of the ocean.
Could simple **creatures** survive on Mars?
The story is about a small green **creature** with three eyes.

creature.note: **Creature** is used for animals and imaginary beings, not normally for plants and not for people (except in phrases like *a creature of habit*).

senses.en: to continue to live, especially after a difficult or dangerous situation
examples: No plant could **survive** without water.
All the passengers **survived** the crash.
Some tiny creatures can **survive** in extremely cold places.

forms.en: the state of continuing to live
forms.vi: sự sống sót, sự sinh tồn
forms.ex: Water is necessary for the **survival** of every living thing.

forms.en: a person who continues to live after an accident or disaster
forms.ex: Rescue teams found three **survivors** in the building.

senses.en: to travel through a place in order to learn about it
examples: Robots are sent to **explore** the surface of Mars.
We spent the morning **exploring** the old town.
Humans have not **explored** most of the ocean.

senses.en: to think about or examine an idea carefully
examples: The class **explored** the question of life on other planets.
We should **explore** every possible solution.
Her essay **explores** why people are afraid of the dark.

forms.en: the act of travelling through a place or studying something to learn about it
forms.vi: sự thám hiểm, sự khám phá
forms.ex: Space **exploration** costs a lot of money.

forms.en: a person who travels to unknown places to find out about them
forms.ex: The **explorer** wrote a book about her journey.

senses.en: to send a rocket, spacecraft or missile up into the sky or into space
examples: They will **launch** the rocket at six o'clock tomorrow.
The satellite was **launched** from an island near the equator.
Bad weather stopped them from **launching** the spacecraft.

senses.en: to start something new, such as a product, a campaign or a plan
examples: The company will **launch** its new phone in May.
Our school **launched** a project to clean the river.
She **launched** a website about astronomy.

senses.en: the act of sending a spacecraft into space, or of starting something new
examples: We watched the **launch** live on television.
The **launch** of the new book is next Friday.

senses.en: the Sun together with the planets and other objects that travel around it
examples: Jupiter is the largest planet in the **solar system**.
Our **solar system** formed billions of years ago.
Scientists have found other **solar systems** far away.

solar system.note: Normally used with **the**: *the solar system*, *the planets of the solar system*. The adjective **solar** means *of the Sun*, as in *solar energy* and *solar panels*.

senses.en: a very large group of stars and planets held together in space
examples: Our **galaxy** is called the Milky Way.
There are billions of **galaxies** in the universe.
The telescope photographed a **galaxy** far from Earth.

galaxy.note: When we mean our own galaxy we say **the galaxy**. The plural is *galaxies* (y → ies). Do not confuse **galaxy** (one group of stars) with **universe** (everything that exists).
